fatal_errors: The proposed W-Mo-Ti-Cr composition and SLM route do not reconstruct the MgAlTiVFeCo powder/SPS system.
A W- and Mo-rich refractory alloy conflicts with the lightweight requirement.

The cited studies concern NbMoTaW made by SLM, WVTaTiCr coatings made by laser cladding, or WMoTaNb alloys; none directly validates SLM-processed W-Mo-Ti-Cr with the claimed phase constitution and properties.
The claimed Laves-phase precipitation, heat-treatment response, oxidation resistance, and aqueous corrosion resistance are unsupported by the cited evidence.
The proposed temperature boundary of 1600 °C misses the relevant 800–1000 °C SPS window and does not address magnesium volatilization or the minimum densification temperature.

The falsification experiment tests only broad performance against unrelated superalloys and cannot distinguish solid-solution/precipitation hardening from densification, defect reduction, or passive-film mechanisms.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses hardness, oxidation, and corrosion only at a broad thematic level. It misses the target composition, initial ball-milled BCC powder, SPS intervention, processing window, oxide barrier phases, passive-film mechanism, and the specified oxidation and corrosion environments. It also supplies no quantitative predictions corresponding to relative density, microhardness, oxidation rate constants, or electrochemical parameters. The evidence is largely analogical and spans different compositions and processing methods, so it cannot establish phase stability or the proposed Laves-phase mechanism for W-Mo-Ti-Cr. A useful discriminating test would compare SPS temperatures within 800–1000 °C and correlate density and oxide-phase distribution with parabolic oxidation constants and NaCl electrochemical parameters.
